description: Faithful reproduction of OpenClaw's agent-side architecture for CUA. Six components (B1-B6) across three phases: Phase 1 builds independent modules (prompt builder, memory, session persistence), Phase 2 adds context management and tool wiring, Phase 3 integrates everything into the agent loop. IMPORTANT: Category C components (CUA SDK callbacks like ImageRetentionCallback, TrajectorySaverCallback, BudgetManagerCallback, PromptInstructionsCallback) are assumed directly reusable from the CUA SDK without modification. This assumption may be wrong — these callbacks may have undocumented constraints, incompatible hook signatures, ordering dependencies, or behavioral quirks when combined with our custom callbacks. Every story that uses a Category C component must verify it works as expected during integration, not just assume it. If a CUA callback doesn't behave as needed, file an issue and implement a workaround or replacement in agents/openclaw/ rather than patching the CUA SDK.

userStories.notes: Closes four gaps vs OpenClaw: (1) Prior messages not replayed — currently each ComputerAgent.run() starts with only the instruction string; OpenClaw replays full transcript as API messages. Fix: load_history() → build_replay_messages() → pass as messages arg to agent.run(). CUA's ComputerAgent.run(messages) already accepts a message list that becomes old_items in the loop. (2) Compaction summary as instruction vs message — currently summaries are prepended to instruction string via _create_compacted_instruction(); OpenClaw injects them as real messages replacing pre-compaction entries. Fix: convert compaction entries to assistant messages in the replay. (3) Cross-run relies on memory system only — TASK_MEMORY.md bootstrap + memory_search/get are the only bridges; the model never sees prior turns as conversation. Fix: transcript replay gives the model actual prior context. (4) No history sanitization — OpenClaw has a pipeline (repair tool pairings, drop thinking blocks, strip stale usage, validate images, limit turns). Fix: implement sanitize_history() + limit_history_turns() applied before replay. Key files: agents/openclaw/session.py (add build_replay_messages, sanitize_history, limit_history_turns), openclaw_agent.py (wire replay into perform_task before agent.run()).

userStories.title: Budget-Aware Compaction Split
userStories.description: As the agent harness, I want the compaction pipeline's half-split replaced with a budget-aware split that calculates available space for kept messages, so that kept message replay (US-OC-012) doesn't cause cascading compaction from context budget pressure.

context.depends: US-OC-012 must be done first (budget pressure only manifests when kept messages are replayed)
context.reference: openclaw/src/agents/compaction.ts (compaction-safeguard extension adjusts split point for budget); openclaw/src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compact.ts (Pi SDK split logic)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Unit tests pass — split point calculated as available_for_kept = context_window - instructions_tokens - summary_estimate - margin; split adapts when instructions are large
Level 1: Unit tests pass — repairToolUseResultPairing() fixes orphaned tool_use/tool_result pairs at split boundary
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 100 with CONTEXT_WINDOW_OVERRIDE=50000 — no cascading compaction (compaction_count stays <= 2)
userStories.notes: PRD Group A (from US-OC-006 design review). Three coupled changes: (1) Replace naive half-split with budget calculation. (2) Add repairToolUseResultPairing() for kept messages — chunk_messages_by_token_share can split between tool_use and its result, API rejects orphaned tool_results. (3) Wire with US-OC-012's kept message replay. OpenClaw does NOT split by half — Pi SDK decides the split point internally, and the compaction-safeguard extension adjusts if budget is exceeded.

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)

ONLY output the structured summary.'); initial summarize_chunk call (no previous_summary) uses SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT with <conversation> tag wrapping; update call (with previous_summary) uses UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT with both <conversation> and <previous-summary> tag wrapping
Level 1: MERGE_SUMMARIES_INSTRUCTIONS constant and _merge_summaries() function removed from context.py

userStories.notes: The three prompt constants to adopt from @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent: (1) SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT — strict 'do not continue, ONLY output structured summary' framing; (2) SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT — structured format with Goal/Constraints/Progress/Key Decisions/Next Steps/Critical Context sections; (3) UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT — distinct update prompt used when previous_summary exists, with explicit rules to preserve/add/move items. Drop MERGE_SUMMARIES_INSTRUCTIONS/_merge_summaries() — these were workarounds for unstructured prose that are no longer needed. See plan doc for full prompt texts and the summarize_chunk() update spec.

userStories.notes: PRD Group B (from US-OC-006 design review). CUA's PromptInstructionsCallback and ImageRetentionCallback modify messages before API calls. Our transcript captures what CUA yields (output items), not what it sends (preprocessed messages). For replay fidelity, we need the actual API-facing messages. The ContextOverflowCallback already receives the full payload in on_llm_start — extend it to persist these messages.

userStories.title: Multi-Stage Summarization for Scale
userStories.description: As the agent harness, I want a multi-stage summarization strategy (split-summarize-merge) alongside iterative rolling summarization, so that 500+ step tasks don't overwhelm the summarization prompt with accumulated context.

context.reference: openclaw/src/agents/compaction.ts (summarizeInStages — the multi-stage pattern)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: Unit tests pass — summarize_in_stages splits chunks into groups, summarizes each group, then merges group summaries
Level 1: Unit tests pass — strategy selection: iterative for <= 10 chunks, multi-stage for > 10 chunks
Level 2: Synthetic test with 500+ messages — multi-stage produces coherent summary without context overflow in summarization calls
userStories.notes: PRD Group C (from US-OC-006 design review). For 500+ step tasks, iterative rolling summarization accumulates summary context across many chunks — the accumulated summary may compete for space in the summarization prompt. OpenClaw's summarizeInStages splits chunks into groups of ~5, summarizes each group independently, then merges the group summaries. Add this as an alternative strategy, auto-selected when chunk count exceeds a threshold.

userStories.title: Custom Loop Architecture Exploration
userStories.description: As the project lead, I want an investigation of CUA's custom_loop parameter as an alternative to stop-compact-resume, so that I can decide whether mid-conversation compaction is feasible without breaking out of the agent loop.

context.reference: submodules/cua/libs/python/agent/agent/agent.py (custom_loop implementation)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Document findings in docs/plan/US-OC-017-custom-loop-exploration.md
Level 1: Prototype custom_loop that manages a mutable message list and supports mid-loop compaction injection
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 50 with custom_loop — agent completes task without stop-compact-resume; compaction happens mid-conversation
Level 2: Compare trajectory quality: custom_loop vs stop-compact-resume on same task
userStories.notes: PRD Group D (from US-OC-006 design review). CUA's on_llm_start callback output is discarded after each turn — the agent loop always re-concatenates from immutable old_items + new_items. This makes callback-based compaction impossible. A custom_loop could manage its own mutable message list, enabling OpenClaw-style mid-conversation compaction without the state discontinuity of stop-compact-resume. This is an exploration story — the outcome may be 'not feasible' if custom_loop has constraints we don't yet see.

userStories.notes: ThinkingConfig defines mode presets that map to budget_tokens values. Explicit --thinking-budget overrides the preset. ComputerAgent passes **additional_generation_kwargs through to the Anthropic loop's predict_step, which spreads **kwargs into litellm.acompletion() — so passing thinking={type: enabled, budget_tokens: N} flows through without CUA SDK changes. Both initial ComputerAgent (line 250) and post-compaction rebuild (line 631) must receive the same thinking params. ThinkingConfig also has optional flush_mode and compaction_mode fields (default 'off') consumed by US-OC-020.

userStories.title: Thinking Mode: Wire into Memory Flush and Compaction
userStories.description: As a benchmark operator, I want per-call-site thinking config for memory flush and compaction LLM calls so that these auxiliary summarization calls can use a different (typically lighter) thinking mode than the main loop.

existingFiles: submodules/cua/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/openclaw_agent.py (_run_memory_flush line 528 — direct litellm.acompletion; _compact_and_rebuild line 601 — calls compact_messages)

context.reference: submodules/cua/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/openclaw/context.py (start from _summarize_chunk at line 573 for the litellm.acompletion call pattern)

acceptanceCriteria: Level 1: Lint passes (uv run ruff check .)
Level 1: _run_memory_flush passes thinking API params to litellm.acompletion when flush_mode is not off
Level 1: compact_messages and its _summarize_chunk/_final_summary accept and pass thinking params when compaction_mode is not off
Level 1: Unit test: ThinkingConfig(mode='deep', flush_mode='light', compaction_mode='off') produces correct API params for each call site
Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 50 with --thinking-mode deep and CONTEXT_WINDOW_OVERRIDE=50000 — compaction triggers and completes without error
userStories.notes: Memory flush and compaction are summarization tasks that typically benefit less from deep thinking. Both default to 'off' even when the main loop uses thinking. CLI flags --flush-thinking-mode and --compaction-thinking-mode are not needed now — code-level config via ThinkingConfig fields is sufficient. The key change is threading thinking params through compact_messages → _summarize_chunk/_final_summary, which currently only accept model and max_tokens.
